content:
Sean Gallagher: Dropping here for SRE review: proposed Private min-pack alert rules + severity mapping. We need to lock paging policy this week so Sergio can finish the PrometheusRule bundle. Current draft is in the working spec + PR branch.

Sean Gallagher: Links:
- Working spec section “Alerting philosophy + thresholds”: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PRIVATE/Private+Observability+Min+Pack+-+Working+Spec
- Draft rules PR (observability-pack): https://github.com/redwoodinference/observability-pack/pull/322

Sergio Costa: thx. high-level: I tried to keep it to burn-rate + a few “something is on fire” infra alerts. But I’m worried we’re still noisy on resource exhaustion.

Allison Grant: +1 to reviewing now. Reminder: “minimum pack” != “everything we can measure”. Baseline should be low-noise, actionable, and map to supported runbooks.

Vivek Kulkarni: Product angle: we’re telling customers “day-1 usable”. If paging is too aggressive we’ll create a bad first impression (and support load). But we also can’t miss outages.

Sean Gallagher: Proposed routing:
- sev1 = page 24/7 (OnCall-SRE) + auto-create incident channel when firing >10m
- sev2 = page business hours (or page 24/7 only for dedicated enterprise tiers?)
- sev3 = ticket only (Support queue)
For Private we should default to “SRE page for sev1 only” and everything else ticket unless customer explicitly opts into paging.

Dev Patel: +1 on “ticket unless sev1”. Support can take the early triage if we have the dashboards + checklist. But we need consistent labels so Alertmanager can route.

Sergio Costa: Current labels in the rules:
- severity: critical|warning
- team: sre|private-deployments
- component: gateway|runtime|control-plane|pipeline
If we want sev1/sev2/sev3 explicitly, I can rename `severity` or add `paging=page|ticket`.

Allison Grant: Please don’t overload `severity`. If we keep `severity` as critical/warn and add `paging` as page/ticket, we can route consistently across installs. Also easier to explain in docs.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. Use:
- `severity`: critical|warning
- `paging`: page|ticket
- `service`: gateway|runtime|installer|prometheus|grafana|vector
…and keep `team`.

Nadia Rahman: Also pls avoid label dimensions that explode cardinality for alert instances. Anything per-tenant/per-route/per-model needs very careful grouping.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. Some of the runtime rules are per `model` right now. That will page a lot when customers have a zoo of models.

Sergio Costa: Yeah, guilty. I had an alert like “KV cache hit rate tanked for model X” which is interesting but not baseline.

Sean Gallagher: Hard line from SRE: no per-model pages in the minimum pack. We can have dashboards that slice by model, but alerts should generally be aggregate (maybe per-cluster or per-service) unless it’s a single dominant “active_model” signal.

Logan Wright: On burn-rate: what SLOs are we standardizing for Private? We should align on a small set that map to “supported”.

Allison Grant: Draft “supported SLOs” for Private min pack:
1) Gateway request success (availability): 99.9% over 30d (HTTP or gRPC mapped)
2) Gateway latency (p99) objective: customer-specific; we can’t enforce a universal number. Use error budget burn on “slow requests” only if we have a defined threshold.
3) Runtime saturation: not an SLO; alert as infra health (ticket by default)
4) Observability pipeline health: must-have, but ticket unless it’s “no metrics/logs at all”

Sean Gallagher: For now, let’s do SLO burn alerts only on availability (5xx + transport errors). Latency hard-threshold pages are always customer-specific and will be noisy. Latency can be “ticket” w/ conservative defaults.

Sergio Costa: Ok. Availability SLO burn windows: I used the standard pair:
- fast burn: 5m / 1h
- slow burn: 30m / 6h
And both require “for: 10m” to avoid flapping.

Sean Gallagher: Good. For Private, set `paging=page` only for:
- Availability fast burn (5m/1h) critical
- “All traffic failing” / “Gateway down” / “No endpoints reachable” class
Everything else default ticket.

Bruno Silva: Question: should “Prometheus rules not loaded” be page? We had that drill where promtool passed but the PrometheusRule CRD didn’t reconcile.

Allison Grant: That’s a good one. If rules aren’t loaded, we’re blind. But do we want to page Redwood SRE for customer-managed Prometheus? In many installs, we don’t own their Prom.

Sean Gallagher: Exactly. For customer-managed Prometheus/Grafana, we should not page Redwood on “rules not loaded” unless they opted into managed mode. Default should be ticket with clear action: “operator check PrometheusRule status / logs”.

Dev Patel: +1. Make it a ticket with a very explicit error message + link to runbook section. Otherwise support gets 20 pings with no context.

Sergio Costa: I can split pipeline/management alerts into two categories:
- “Missing signals (hard)” = we’re not scraping gateway/runtime at all
- “Missing signals (soft)” = partial scrape gaps
Hard could be page only when Redwood-managed Prom is in use; else ticket.

Nadia Rahman: How are you detecting “missing signals”? Please don’t do `absent()` per label dimension. That can explode.

Sergio Costa: Current approach (draft) is aggregated absent on job/service only:
```promql
absent(up{job=~"redwood-gateway|redwood-runtime"} == 1)
```
And for metrics presence, a single “heartbeat” metric we can emit from each component.

Omar El-Sayed: Heartbeat metric is good. For runtime we can use `redwood_runtime_build_info` (1) + `up`, but build_info may exist even if traffic isn’t flowing.

Allison Grant: Standard wants a dedicated heartbeat counter/gauge with stable labels (cluster, service, instance) only. No route/model/tenant.

Sean Gallagher: Cool. Back to resource exhaustion alerts: what do we have currently?

Sergio Costa: Draft includes (all currently `warning`):
- GPU utilization sustained > 95% (15m)
- GPU memory near full > 95% (15m)
- CPU throttling high
- Node disk pressure
- Queue depth high (runtime scheduler)
- Vector/Fluent Bit drops/backpressure

Sean Gallagher: GPU util >95% is not an alert by itself. That’s normal under load. It should be a dashboard signal.

Allison Grant: +1. Alert should be on symptom + saturation + inability to recover. Example: queue depth growing + p99 latency burning + error rate. But those are multi-signal and hard to do generically.

Sean Gallagher: Minimum pack: keep resource alerts to “imminent failure” only:
- Disk filling (predict linear time-to-full < 24h) -> ticket
- OOMKills / container restarts spike -> ticket, page only if it impacts availability
- GPU memory ECC / Xid errors (if exposed) -> ticket
Avoid “utilization high” paging.

Sergio Costa: Got it. I’ll remove pure-utilization alerts, keep “node disk will fill” + “pods crashlooping” style, and keep them ticket.

Logan Wright: What about “Vector dropping logs” / “export failing”? Some customers care a lot.

Sean Gallagher: Make pipeline alerts ticket, except “no logs/metrics for X minutes” could be sev1 *if* it coincides with active incident? Otherwise you’ll page at 3am because someone rotated creds for their SIEM.

Dev Patel: If we can include the destination in the alert annotation (e.g., `sink=siem`) it helps. But again, keep label cardinality controlled.

Sergio Costa: Will do via annotation only (templated message), not label.

Allison Grant: Severity mapping proposal for docs:
- `paging=page` + `severity=critical`: immediate action, Redwood on-call engaged (only used for SLO fast burn + total outage)
- `paging=ticket` + `severity=critical`: urgent operator action needed, but not paging by default
- `severity=warning`: investigate during business hours / capacity planning

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also, add `runbook_url` annotations everywhere. If we ship alerts with no runbook, support will suffer.

Sergio Costa: Already adding `runbook_url` + `summary` + `description`. Example (draft):
```yaml
annotations:
  summary: "Gateway availability error budget burn (fast)"
  description: "High 5xx/transport error rate is consuming the 30d error budget quickly. Check gateway dashboard + upstream runtime health."
  runbook_url: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PRIVATE/Runbook+Gateway+Availability"
```

Bruno Silva: One more: please keep rule group names stable. Installer is going to toggle groups based on values.yaml (`alerts.groups.gateway=true`, etc). If we rename groups each release, upgrades will be messy.

Sergio Costa: Ack. I’ll keep group names stable: `minpack-slo`, `minpack-pipeline`, `minpack-infra`, `minpack-controlplane`.

Nadia Rahman: Final request: wherever you have `by (...)` please sanity check label sets. Also ensure we don’t include `route` or `tenant` in alert grouping.

Sean Gallagher: Action items:
1) Sergio: update rules to add `paging` label + remove pure utilization alerts; no per-model alerts; keep only aggregate.
2) Allison: write down the final mapping guidance for docs (severity/paging definitions) + what is “supported by default”.
3) Sean: review updated PR + confirm which alerts are allowed to page.

Vivek Kulkarni: +1. Once this is locked I’ll align messaging in the PRD: “minimum pack pages only on hard downtime; everything else is ticket + dashboards.”

Sergio Costa: cool, I’ll push updates to PR-322 today and ping back here for final sign-off.

Sean Gallagher: thx. (reactions: Allison Grant :thumbsup:, Dev Patel :thumbsup:, Nadia Rahman :eyes:)
